title: FirstStrike Research: brand identity / Timothy Ali
text:
FIRSTSTRIKE RESEARCH
FIRSTSTRIKE RESEARCH

FirstStrike Research is a veteran-owned financial research blog about American markets. I designed its logo, colors, type, and brand guidelines.

ROLE
Sole brand designer
TOOLS
Illustrator, Figma
01 / 05
THE BRIEF

The client brought a rough mood board of retro print references and wanted the brand to feel direct and credible. From there I worked out a heavy wordmark, halftone details, and a blue palette.

02 / 05
LOGO & WORDMARK

The wordmark uses heavy italic type with a halftone pattern trailing off the F. The forward lean suits the name, and the dots bring in the newsprint reference from the brief.

I made horizontal and stacked lockups, plus an icon for favicons and avatars. Each has versions for light and dark backgrounds.

03 / 05
COLOR & TYPE

Electric Blue (#003DFF) is the main color, with Midnight Black and Ice White. Soft Mint, Signal Coral, and Amber Pulse widen the palette for charts and graphics. Headlines are in Helvetica Heavy and body copy in Helvetica Medium.

04 / 05
PRINT TEXTURE

I added grain to a blue-to-cyan gradient for a printed texture, then used it across social cards, editorial layouts, and billboard mockups.

05 / 05
OUTCOME

I handed over the logo files and guidelines for color, typography, and backgrounds, with examples on business cards, social graphics, and billboards.

NEXT / [07]
DO ANDROIDS DREAM? ->

title: Toolbox: desktop app for brand files / Timothy Ali
text:
TOOLBOX
TOOLBOX

I designed and built Toolbox for the file prep that comes with brand work. It packages logos for print and web, exports color palettes, makes type specimens, and converts images. It runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and every tool also works from the command line or through an AI assistant over MCP.

ROLE
Designer & developer
TIMELINE
Started August 2026; rebuilt in Rust for version 1.2.0, October 2026
TOOLS
Rust, Tauri, Leptos, Claude Code
LIVE
Downloads and guides
->
01 / 03
FOUR TOOLS

Lockup turns logo SVGs into a folder of print and web files. You get color, black, and white versions in several sizes, a README, and social images if you want them. PDF and EPS exports can carry named Pantone spot colors. Palette turns a set of colors into code, swatches, and reference sheets. Specimen makes type sheets from your installed fonts, and Convert changes image formats, sizes, and compression.

Projects keep each client or job together. You can save the settings, reopen the work later, and export it again. Every export goes in a new folder, so earlier deliveries are left alone. The library and the exported files stay on your computer.

Palette extracts colors from artwork. Specimen previews a type sheet.

Convert shows the output size for each format. The app opens on your projects.

02 / 03
APP, COMMAND LINE, AND AGENTS

The command line and the MCP server take the same settings as the app, so a script or an AI assistant can inspect source files, preview results, reopen saved work, and export without opening a window.

An assistant can also sort a client folder. It plans the moves, and Toolbox checks them, shows a dry run first, and keeps an undo record. Nothing gets deleted.

The app shares its terminal look and several components with this site.

03 / 03
OUTCOME

Version 1.2.0 is the first one built in Rust, with Tauri and Leptos instead of Electron and Svelte. I kept the old app as the reference and only deleted it once the new one matched it.

I also took out the chat window and the AI built into the app. I drive Toolbox from my own model over MCP now, so organizing folders became MCP and command-line tools. The app opens on your projects, and every tool has a smooth or hard edges setting.

Toolbox is available for macOS, Windows, and Linux. The macOS builds are signed and notarized, and Linux builds come as AppImage and deb packages. I dropped Windows at 1.1.0 because of the cost of code signing. It’s back in 1.2.0, unsigned. Downloads and guides are on this site.

Lockup turns logo SVGs into a folder of print and web files. You get color, black, and white versions in several sizes, a README, and social images if you want them. PDF and EPS exports can carry named Pantone spot colors. Palette turns a set of colors into code, swatches, and reference sheets. Specimen makes type sheets from your installed fonts, and Convert changes image formats, sizes, and compression.

Projects keep each client or job together. You can save the settings, reopen the work later, and export it again. Every export goes in a new folder, so earlier deliveries are left alone. The library and the exported files stay on your computer.

PALETTE EXTRACTS COLORS FROM ARTWORK. SPECIMEN PREVIEWS A TYPE SHEET.

CONVERT SHOWS THE OUTPUT SIZE FOR EACH FORMAT. THE APP OPENS ON YOUR PROJECTS.

02 / 03
APP, COMMAND LINE, AND AGENTS

The command line and the MCP server take the same settings as the app, so a script or an AI assistant can inspect source files, preview results, reopen saved work, and export without opening a window.

An assistant can also sort a client folder. It plans the moves, and Toolbox checks them, shows a dry run first, and keeps an undo record. Nothing gets deleted.

The app shares its terminal look and several components with this site.

03 / 03
OUTCOME

Version 1.2.0 is the first one built in Rust, with Tauri and Leptos instead of Electron and Svelte. I kept the old app as the reference and only deleted it once the new one matched it.

I also took out the chat window and the AI built into the app. I drive Toolbox from my own model over MCP now, so organizing folders became MCP and command-line tools. The app opens on your projects, and every tool has a smooth or hard edges setting.

Toolbox is available for macOS, Windows, and Linux. The macOS builds are signed and notarized, and Linux builds come as AppImage and deb packages. I dropped Windows at 1.1.0 because of the cost of code signing. It’s back in 1.2.0, unsigned. Downloads and guides are on this site.

LOCKUP
LOCKUP

Turn your logo variations into a set of print and web files.

IN
Vector SVGs
OUT
PNG, JPEG, SVG, PDF, EPS, README
GET IT
Download for macOS, Windows, or Linux
->
WHEN TO USE IT

Lockup is for preparing a set of logo files for a client, developer, or printer. Add an SVG for each logo variation, then pick the formats, colors, and sizes you need. You can assign CMYK and Pantone print colors in the app, the CLI, or MCP. For one-off image conversions, use Convert.

EXPORTED FILES

You get WEB and PRINT folders, sorted by logo variation, color treatment, and size, plus a README that explains what’s in them. Web files come as PNG, JPEG, and SVG, and print files as JPEG, PDF, and EPS.

CLI & MCP

Set up the toolbox command using the linked guide, then run this example with your own inputs. The options below work with both the CLI and MCP.

toolbox lockup logo.svg --print none --padding 0.1 --out .

EXPORTED FILES

You get WEB and PRINT folders, sorted by logo variation, color treatment, and size, plus a README that explains what’s in them. Web files come as PNG, JPEG, and SVG, and print files as JPEG, PDF, and EPS.

CLI & MCP

Set up the toolbox command using the linked guide, then run this example with your own inputs. The options below work with both the CLI and MCP.

toolbox lockup logo.svg --print none --padding 0.1 --out .
--action <export|inspect|preview|library-list|library-get|library-remove>
Export files, inspect settings and the output plan without writing, render previews, or manage saved work. Convert previews write the selected output formats; other tools write PNG. Specimen also lists fonts. Default: export.
--saved <value>
Saved-work ID to reopen. Explicit options override its settings. Required for library-get and library-remove.
--save
Save the completed export to the app library, or update the reopened record. Defaults to false for scripts. Default: false.
--name <value>
Package name used in the folder and file names.
--variations <json>

CLI & MCP

Set up the toolbox command using the linked guide, then run this example with your own inputs. The options below work with both the CLI and MCP.

toolbox palette '#D32F05' '#003A5D' --name Acme --out .
--action <export|inspect|preview|library-list|library-get|library-remove>
Export files, inspect settings and the output plan without writing, render previews, or manage saved work. Convert previews write the selected output formats; other tools write PNG. Specimen also lists fonts. Default: export.
--saved <value>
Saved-work ID to reopen. Explicit options override its settings. Required for library-get and library-remove.
--save
Save the completed export to the app library, or update the reopened record. Defaults to false for scripts. Default: false.
--entries <json>
Ordered swatches as JSON: [{"name":"Orange","hex":"#D32F05","cmyk":[0,78,98,17],"pantone":"1665 C"}]. Replaces extracted or saved entries; colors and samples then append.
--samples <json>
Sample image colors at normalized coordinates: [{"image":0,"x":0.5,"y":0.5}]. Image indices come from inspect.
--extract
Add dominant image colors automatically. Disable to select only explicit samples or entries. Default: true.
--colors <values…>
Hex colours to include, for example ['#D32F05', '#003A5D']. You can supply these values without --colors.
--input <values…>
Paths of artwork to pull colours from. SVGs contribute their exact fills; images contribute their dominant colours. Combines with `colors`.
--name <value>
Palette name, used for the file names and the sheet heading. Default: Palette.
--outputs <css|tokens|ase|sheet>
Which files to write. Default: css, tokens, ase, sheet.
--edgeSmoothing <smooth|hard>
Edges on the swatch sheet (PNG, and the image inside its PDF): 'smooth' anti-aliases them; 'hard' turns anti-aliasing off. Default: smooth.
--out <value>
Folder to write into. A fresh subfolder is created inside it, so nothing is overwritten. Required for export and preview.

title: CLI & MCP / Toolbox / Timothy Ali
text:
CLI & MCP
CLI & MCP

Use Toolbox from a terminal or an AI assistant.

Toolbox includes a command-line interface (CLI) and an MCP server. Use the CLI in your terminal or scripts. MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets an AI assistant find and run the tools. Both work without opening an app window.

SET UP
COMMAND LINE
ADVANCED
OPTIONS
LIST
RUN
SERVE
ORGANIZE
MACOS
/Applications/Toolbox.app/Contents/MacOS/Toolbox
LINUX
toolbox
SET UP THE COMMAND

Install Toolbox first. You can run it from the full executable path shown above, or set up the toolbox shortcut these examples use. On macOS, the command here creates that shortcut. Run the executable directly. The macOS open command won’t send results back to your terminal.

sudo ln -s "/Applications/Toolbox.app/Contents/MacOS/Toolbox" /usr/local/bin/toolbox
THE COMMAND LINE

Choose a tool, add your inputs and options, and set an output folder. Running toolbox without arguments opens the app. The CLI and MCP support all four tools and the same export settings.

toolbox help
# show tools and usage
toolbox convert --help
# show Convert options
toolbox --version
# show the version
toolbox lockup logo.svg --print none --padding 0.1 --out .
toolbox palette '#D32F05' '#003A5D' --name Acme --out .
toolbox specimen --template classic --family Helvetica --out .
toolbox convert a.heic b.png --formats webp --compression 40 --out ~/Desktop
INPUTS
Pass file paths to convert and lockup, or hex colors to palette, without a flag. Relative paths start from your current folder. Put quotes around paths with spaces.
LISTS AND SWITCHES
Separate values with spaces or commas: --formats webp png or --formats=webp,png. Use none to skip a group (--print none) and --no- to turn a switch off (--no-social).
OUTPUT
--out writes into a new folder inside the destination, leaving existing files alone. Add --json for a JSON result. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 failed, 2 invalid; errors go to stderr.
ADVANCED

From version 1.1.0 you can also assign print colors, adjust logo variations, and set font roles. Structured flags like --palette and --roles take a JSON array in quotes. Over MCP, pass the same arrays without quotes. Use inspect to find the colors in your artwork and fonts to list installed families.

--action inspect shows what will be exported without writing files. --action preview with --out saves previews. Add --save to keep the settings in the app’s library, then reopen them with the savedID in the result.

Version 1.2.0 adds --edgeSmoothing to every tool. hard turns off anti-aliasing in the raster files, so every pixel is fully in or out. Vector files don’t change. smooth is the default.

toolbox lockup logo.svg --action inspect --json
toolbox lockup logo.svg --name Acme --out ./exports --palette '[{"sourceHex":"#D32F05","cmyk":[0,78,98,17],"pantone":"1665 C"}]'
toolbox specimen --action fonts --json
toolbox specimen --title "Acme type" --out ./exports --roles '[{"label":"Heading","family":"Helvetica","face":"Bold","size":40}]'
toolbox lockup logo.svg --edgeSmoothing hard --out ./exports
toolbox lockup logo.svg --print none --save --out ./exports --json
toolbox lockup --action library-list --json
toolbox lockup --saved RECORD_ID --action inspect --json
toolbox lockup --saved RECORD_ID --padding 0.15 --save --out ./exports --json
OPTIONS

Each tool’s page lists its flags and defaults. To check your installed version, run toolbox <tool> --help, or toolbox list for the option schemas as JSON.

LOCKUP OPTIONS
->
PALETTE OPTIONS
->
SPECIMEN OPTIONS
->
CONVERT OPTIONS
->
LIST

Run toolbox list to get a JSON catalog of all four tools and the organize steps, with descriptions, argument schemas, and examples. For one tool, run toolbox describe and the tool’s name.

toolbox list
# every tool, as JSON
toolbox describe convert
# one tool, as JSON
RUN

Pass the tool name and arguments to --run as a JSON object. Toolbox returns the output folder, file names, and any warnings. A failed job returns "ok": false with an error message and exits with code 1. Replace the example paths with your own.

toolbox --run '{"tool":"convert","args":{
  "input":["/Users/me/Pictures/IMG_0001.heic"],
  "formats":["webp"],
  "compression":40,
  "longestEdge":2000,
  "out":"/Users/me/Desktop"
}}'
{
  "ok": true,
  "tool": "convert",
  "outputDir": "/Users/me/Desktop/Converted",
  "files": ["IMG_0001.webp"],
  "warnings": []
}
SERVE

To connect an AI assistant, add this server configuration to its MCP settings, using the executable path for your platform. --mcp serves the tools over standard input and output. Claude Code reads project settings from .mcp.json.

Then ask your assistant to convert screenshots to WebP, package logo SVGs, pull colors from artwork, or tidy a client folder. Tell it where the source files are and which folder to save to.

toolbox --mcp
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "toolbox": {
      "command": "/Applications/Toolbox.app/Contents/MacOS/Toolbox",
      "args": ["--mcp"]
    }
  }
}
ORGANIZE A FOLDER

Toolbox can sort a client folder, but it doesn’t decide where things go. Your assistant plans the moves. Toolbox lists the folder, checks the plan, moves the files, and keeps a record so you can undo it. Over MCP the steps are organize_scan, organize_apply, organize_undo, and organize_history. In a terminal they’re toolbox organize scan, apply, undo, and history. Each one prints JSON.

toolbox organize scan ~/Clients/Acme
toolbox organize apply ~/Clients/Acme --dryRun \
  --moves '[{"from":"IMG_0042.jpg","to":"Photos/IMG_0042.jpg"}]' \
  --keep '[{"path":"logo.svg"}]'
toolbox organize apply ~/Clients/Acme \
  --moves '[{"from":"IMG_0042.jpg","to":"Photos/IMG_0042.jpg"}]' \
  --keep '[{"path":"logo.svg"}]'
toolbox organize history ~/Clients/Acme
toolbox organize undo JOURNAL_ID
1. SCAN
Lists what’s in the folder, numbered, with duplicate files grouped. Nothing moves.
2. DRY RUN
Send the planned moves with --dryRun, or dryRun: true over MCP. Toolbox checks them and changes nothing. Show the user the result.
3. APPLY
Only after they agree, send the same plan without --dryRun. Toolbox checks the folder again first and leaves out any unsafe move, with the reason. Duplicate copies go to a .toolbox-recovery folder inside it. Nothing is deleted.
4. UNDO
Every apply returns a journal ID. toolbox organize undo with that ID puts everything back, and history lists past runs. Undo the newest first.

toolbox lockup logo.svg --edgeSmoothing hard --out ./exports
toolbox lockup logo.svg --print none --save --out ./exports --json
toolbox lockup --action library-list --json
toolbox lockup --saved RECORD_ID --action inspect --json
toolbox lockup --saved RECORD_ID --padding 0.15 --save --out ./exports --json
OPTIONS

Each tool’s page lists its flags and defaults. To check your installed version, run toolbox <tool> --help, or toolbox list for the option schemas as JSON.

LOCKUP OPTIONS
->
PALETTE OPTIONS
->
SPECIMEN OPTIONS
->
CONVERT OPTIONS
->
LIST

Run toolbox list to get a JSON catalog of all four tools and the organize steps, with descriptions, argument schemas, and examples. For one tool, run toolbox describe and the tool’s name.

toolbox list
# every tool, as JSON
toolbox describe convert
# one tool, as JSON
RUN

Pass the tool name and arguments to --run as a JSON object. Toolbox returns the output folder, file names, and any warnings. A failed job returns "ok": false with an error message and exits with code 1. Replace the example paths with your own.

toolbox --run '{"tool":"convert","args":{
  "input":["/Users/me/Pictures/IMG_0001.heic"],
  "formats":["webp"],
  "compression":40,
  "longestEdge":2000,
  "out":"/Users/me/Desktop"
}}'
{
  "ok": true,
  "tool": "convert",
  "outputDir": "/Users/me/Desktop/Converted",
  "files": ["IMG_0001.webp"],
  "warnings": []
}
SERVE

To connect an AI assistant, add this server configuration to its MCP settings, using the executable path for your platform. --mcp serves the tools over standard input and output. Claude Code reads project settings from .mcp.json.

Then ask your assistant to convert screenshots to WebP, package logo SVGs, pull colors from artwork, or tidy a client folder. Tell it where the source files are and which folder to save to.

toolbox --mcp
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "toolbox": {
      "command": "/Applications/Toolbox.app/Contents/MacOS/Toolbox",
      "args": ["--mcp"]
    }
  }
}
ORGANIZE A FOLDER

Toolbox can sort a client folder, but it doesn’t decide where things go. Your assistant plans the moves. Toolbox lists the folder, checks the plan, moves the files, and keeps a record so you can undo it. Over MCP the steps are organize_scan, organize_apply, organize_undo, and organize_history. In a terminal they’re toolbox organize scan, apply, undo, and history. Each one prints JSON.

toolbox organize scan ~/Clients/Acme
toolbox organize apply ~/Clients/Acme --dryRun \
  --moves '[{"from":"IMG_0042.jpg","to":"Photos/IMG_0042.jpg"}]' \
  --keep '[{"path":"logo.svg"}]'
toolbox organize apply ~/Clients/Acme \
  --moves '[{"from":"IMG_0042.jpg","to":"Photos/IMG_0042.jpg"}]' \
  --keep '[{"path":"logo.svg"}]'
toolbox organize history ~/Clients/Acme
toolbox organize undo JOURNAL_ID
1. SCAN
Lists what’s in the folder, numbered, with duplicate files grouped. Nothing moves.
2. DRY RUN
Send the planned moves with --dryRun, or dryRun: true over MCP. Toolbox checks them and changes nothing. Show the user the result.
3. APPLY
Only after they agree, send the same plan without --dryRun. Toolbox checks the folder again first and leaves out any unsafe move, with the reason. Duplicate copies go to a .toolbox-recovery folder inside it. Nothing is deleted.
4. UNDO
Every apply returns a journal ID. toolbox organize undo with that ID puts everything back, and history lists past runs. Undo the newest first.

text:
CLI & MCP
CLI & MCP

Use Toolbox from a terminal or an AI assistant.

Toolbox includes a command-line interface (CLI) and an MCP server. Use the CLI in your terminal or scripts. MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets an AI assistant find and run the tools. Both work without opening an app window.

SET UP
COMMAND LINE
ADVANCED
OPTIONS
LIST
RUN
SERVE
ORGANIZE
MACOS
/Applications/Toolbox.app/Contents/MacOS/Toolbox
LINUX
toolbox
SET UP THE COMMAND

Install Toolbox first. You can run it from the full executable path shown above, or set up the toolbox shortcut these examples use. On macOS, the command here creates that shortcut. Run the executable directly. The macOS open command won’t send results back to your terminal.

sudo ln -s "/Applications/Toolbox.app/Contents/MacOS/Toolbox" /usr/local/bin/toolbox
THE COMMAND LINE

Choose a tool, add your inputs and options, and set an output folder. Running toolbox without arguments opens the app. The CLI and MCP support all four tools and the same export settings.

toolbox help
# show tools and usage
toolbox convert --help
# show Convert options
toolbox --version
# show the version
toolbox lockup logo.svg --print none --padding 0.1 --out .
toolbox palette '#D32F05' '#003A5D' --name Acme --out .
toolbox specimen --template classic --family Helvetica --out .
toolbox convert a.heic b.png --formats webp --compression 40 --out ~/Desktop
INPUTS
Pass file paths to convert and lockup, or hex colors to palette, without a flag. Relative paths start from your current folder. Put quotes around paths with spaces.
LISTS AND SWITCHES
Separate values with spaces or commas: --formats webp png or --formats=webp,png. Use none to skip a group (--print none) and --no- to turn a switch off (--no-social).
OUTPUT
--out writes into a new folder inside the destination, leaving existing files alone. Add --json for a JSON result. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 failed, 2 invalid; errors go to stderr.
ADVANCED

From version 1.1.0 you can also assign print colors, adjust logo variations, and set font roles. Structured flags like --palette and --roles take a JSON array in quotes. Over MCP, pass the same arrays without quotes. Use inspect to find the colors in your artwork and fonts to list installed families.

--action inspect shows what will be exported without writing files. --action preview with --out saves previews. Add --save to keep the settings in the app’s library, then reopen them with the savedID in the result.

Version 1.2.0 adds --edgeSmoothing to every tool. hard turns off anti-aliasing in the raster files, so every pixel is fully in or out. Vector files don’t change. smooth is the default.

toolbox lockup logo.svg --name Acme --out ./exports --palette '[{"sourceHex":"#D32F05","cmyk":[0,78,98,17],"pantone":"1665 C"}]'
toolbox specimen --action fonts --json
toolbox specimen --title "Acme type" --out ./exports --roles '[{"label":"Heading","family":"Helvetica","face":"Bold","size":40}]'
toolbox lockup logo.svg --edgeSmoothing hard --out ./exports
